memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Judah, your brothers will praise you; your hand will be on the neck of your enemies; your father's sons will bow down to you.'" — Gen 49:8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
After three sons who lost their place, Jacob turns to the fourth — and everything changes.

Judah. The name means praise. And Jacob says his brothers will praise him and bow down to him.

Remember who this man is. Judah proposed selling Joseph for silver (Gen 37:26-27). He walked away from his family and behaved shamefully with Tamar (Gen 38). His record is not clean.

But we have also watched him change. He offered himself as a slave in Benjamin's place (Gen 44:33). He was the one sent ahead to prepare the way into Goshen. Grace had been working on this man for decades.

Leadership in God's family does not go to the flawless — there are none. It goes where God chooses, and God has a habit of choosing people who have been broken and rebuilt.

If your past disqualifies you in your own eyes, look carefully at Judah. The tribe that would carry the promise came from a man who had failed badly and been changed deeply.

God is not looking for people with nothing behind them. He is looking for people who have let Him do something in them.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you believe God can still use you given your history?
2. Where has God been quietly changing you over years?
3. Who have you written off that God may not have?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You do not choose the flawless, because there are none. Keep doing Your patient work in me, and use me despite my history. Amen.
